Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU selection, TPS targets & concurrency clarifications

Hi Helen — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so our infra team can finish the sizing worksheet: 

1) Deployment intent: you confirmed Tidal Health prefers Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) rather than Hosted for PHI workloads; you may evaluate Private (VPC) later.
2) Current pilot targets: 120 TPS peak for generate endpoints (chat + system prompts), average request ~220 tokens in, ~600 tokens out; 70% chat-style messages, 30% bulk-generation jobs.
3) SLA/availability: target 99.9% and 150ms p50 for short-chat requests (<=128 tokens).

Open items for us to confirm:
- Preferred GPU family: do you have a hard requirement (H100 vs A100) or is cost-driven?
- Concurrency per GPU target: are you planning many concurrent users (500+ active sessions) or fewer high-throughput pipelines?
- Cold-start tolerance: are occasional 300–400ms spikes acceptable on cache-miss?

Next steps: Aditya will propose two sizing options (cost-optimized vs latency-optimized) and attach a draft estimate. Can you confirm the TPS and token-mix numbers above or flag changes?

Thanks — Vanessa

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU selection, TPS targets & concurrency clarifications

Thanks Vanessa — brief answers inline: 

- GPU: Procurement prefers H100 if recommended for latency; budget team will review cost delta. If the latency gains are marginal at our token lengths, we can consider A100.
- Concurrency: Our product expects ~250 concurrent active users (web + API), plus 5 sustained batch pipelines that will run at off-peak hours.
- Cold-start: We can tolerate occasional cold-starts up to 400ms, but frequent misses that push p50 >200ms will be a blocker.

I can share more precise token histograms from our analytics next week — that should help with batching/kv-cache assumptions.

— Helen

Hi Helen / Vanessa — pulling together options. A few technical clarifications that will materially change the sizing: 

1) Token mix distribution: can you send percentiles for request sizes (p50/p90/p99) for both input and output tokens? If p90 output is >> 1k tokens, we need to size memory and KV cache differently.

2) KV cache behavior: are you planning to leverage long-lived chat contexts (session affinity) or stateless short chats? Session affinity increases effective throughput per GPU via KV reuse.

3) Latency SLOs by endpoint: you called out 150ms p50 for short-chat — do you have separate SLOs for bulk-generation endpoints? Bulk jobs often accept higher latency and benefit from throughput-oriented batching.

Initial sizing thoughts (ballpark):
- Latency-optimized (H100 80GB): 8 GPUs to hit ~150ms p50 for <=128 token chat at 120 TPS with moderate concurrency and KV cache enabled.
- Cost-optimized (A100 80GB): 10 GPUs with slightly higher p50 (~180–220ms) under same workload but ~20% lower monthly cost.

We can also propose a hybrid pool (mix of H100 for low-latency routes + A100 for background bulk jobs) if that helps balance budget. Attaching a candidate estimate and an SLA draft for procurement review.

If you can share the token histograms, I’ll update the worksheet and include expected p50/p95 numbers per config.

Thanks — Aditya
